INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

2. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

5. D — 100 °C

6. A — newton (N)

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

8. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. A — Ice melting to water

10. B — Producers

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
